FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox imports or test execution against the patched code. In `bench/endocrine.py`, the patched file is written as `tmpdir/<basename(target_path)>`, but the optional test command is executed as the caller-provided `test_cmd` with only `cwd=tmpdir`. No rewrite ensures the test command points at the sandboxed file, and Python import resolution will usually still load modules from the real project tree when tests reference package paths like `bench.endocrine`. Evidence: `patched_path` is never passed into `test_cmd`; no temporary package tree is created; no `PYTHONPATH`/isolated environment is set; only a single file basename is copied to tempdir.
FOLLOW: The advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes (SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL)” capability can report a fix as SAFE/NEUTRAL after running tests against the unmodified source tree, not the patched candidate. That silently corrupts fix verification, which then feeds into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4 where SAFE/NEUTRAL results mark findings as `verified=True`. Downstream consequence: the NK bug-closed gate can close bugs based on falsely verified fixes, causing reviewers to be told a bug is fixed when the tested code was never the patched code.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create a temp directory mirroring the target file’s relative path under the project/package root, write the patched file into that mirrored location, and run tests with an environment that prepends the temp root to `PYTHONPATH` so imports resolve to the sandbox copy before the real source tree.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses aggregate net issue count (`net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`) and treats only positive total as HARMFUL. This misses regressions when one tool worsens and another improves by an equal or larger amount. Evidence: if a patch introduces 3 new pyright errors and removes 5 ruff warnings, `total_net = -2`, so verdict becomes SAFE even though new type errors were introduced. The docstring says “HARMFUL: new issues introduced,” which is stricter than the implemented aggregate test.
FOLLOW: This produces silently wrong fix-evaluation verdicts: fixes that introduce new type/security/lint defects can still be marked SAFE. That directly affects endocrine output and, through the immune pipeline’s Stage 4, can mark bad fixes as `verified=True`. Downstream, the system may close findings on the basis of regressions hidden by aggregate cancellation.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify a fix as HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`); only use aggregate reduction to distinguish SAFE from NEUTRAL when no metric worsened.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the “whole-file replacement” branch in `_apply_fix_to_source()` can replace an arbitrary target file with unrelated valid Python because file identity is not checked. Any proposed fix text that compiles and has at least 5 newlines is accepted as the full replacement. Evidence: after `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")`, the function returns `fix` solely based on `fix.count("\n") >= 5`; it does not verify that the replacement mentions or preserves the target module’s symbols, path, or matched lines.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can become detached from the reported finding and target file: a multi-line prose-ish code block or wrong-module snippet can be written over the sandbox copy and then linted. That yields meaningless SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts not tied to the proposed fix root cause. Because immune stage 4 consumes these verdicts to set `verified=True`, the interface between endocrine and immune can certify irrelevant replacements as verified fixes.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove the whole-file replacement heuristic and only apply fixes when a concrete search/replace or line-targeted transformation succeeds.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_bandit()` invokes `bandit` without recursive/file-target disambiguation, but `scan_health()` passes a list of source files. Bandit CLI commonly expects `-r` for directories and can behave inconsistently for multiple file operands depending on version/wrapper; endocrine assumes JSON `results` will always correspond directly to the requested paths and does no return-code validation. Evidence: `cmd = [BANDIT_BIN, "-f", "json", "-q"] + paths`; unlike ruff/pyright, there is no explicit mode selection or handling for execution failure beyond `NOT_FOUND`.
FOLLOW: Health scans can silently miss security diagnostics or treat execution failures as clean runs, degrading the core “health scan correctly run tools and parse output” feature. Because counts feed the insect brain as structured health signals, reviewers can be shown an artificially healthy security state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — invoke bandit in explicit file mode per file (looping over paths and aggregating JSON results) so execution semantics are stable and failures can be attributed per file.
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring containment. After extracting `*.py` tokens from finding text, it returns the first `source_path` where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. Evidence: the `match in sp_path` clause allows ambiguous partial matches, so a token like `brain.py` can match unrelated longer paths; if multiple files share a basename/suffix, the first one wins with no ambiguity handling.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` may baseline, patch, and score the wrong file. That makes verdicts silently wrong rather than merely unevaluable, which is worse for the PoC because incorrect SAFE/HARMFUL outputs propagate into immune verification and reviewer-facing state. A wrong-file evaluation also undermines the “no source modification” sandbox claim because the sandboxed file may not even be the cited one.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict matching to exact normalized basename or exact suffix path match; if multiple source paths match, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` also marks a tool available when the subprocess times out: each runner returns `[]` on `_run_tool(...).stderr == "TIMEOUT"` because only `"NOT_FOUND"` is special-cased. This means availability is overstated both for missing binaries and for hung tools, so health telemetry can claim a healthy scan from tools that never produced output.

EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is not just a dropped-diagnostics bug. Because `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally, timed-out tools are reported as available and successful, compounding the false health signal.

EXTEND C0005 | The advertised fix-evaluation capability is also partially dead/misleading because test execution is not bound to the patched module under sandbox imports. The feature “fires,” but not necessarily on the modified code, so the capability is operationally incomplete, not just missing categories.
